subject: Learning Methods
title: The Power of Streaks
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Power of Streaks.

hook.text: Jerry Seinfeld wrote jokes every day and marked X on a calendar. His rule: don't break the chain.

buildup.text: Streaks leverage loss aversion. Once you've a 30-day chain, the pain of breaking it outweighs the effort of continuing.

discovery.text: The visual progress is key. Seeing a row of completed days creates a tangible achievement that abstract goals can't.

twist.text: Streaks have a dark side. Missing one day can feel catastrophic, leading to full abandonment.

climax.text: Start a study streak today. Mark it visibly. If you miss a day, resume immediately.

punchline.text: Don't break the chain. But if you do, restart tomorrow.

quiz.question: Why is the rule 'never miss twice' important for maintaining streaks?
options: Two missed days erases all previous learning
One miss is a slip but two misses starts a new habit of not doing it
After two misses, the brain forgets the original habit entirely
